OVERVIEW. The page sets up a long linear expression indexed by a closed cycle of 21 symbols, then tests coefficient-matching conditions for identities between linear polynomials in x. The underlying problem cannot be determined from this page alone; the previous page is a tailor's note and there is no next page.

(A) Indexing. The symbols are the 21 letters a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,k,l,m,n,o,p,q,r,s,t,u,v (j and w omitted). The factors (x-n) show that each letter carries a number:
- c=3, d=4, e=5, f,g,h=6,7,8, i=9, k=10, l=11;
- m,n,o=12,13,14, p=15, q,r=16,17, s=18, t=19, u=20;
- v,a,b=21,22,23.
Since 22≡1 and 23≡2 (mod 21), the letters form a cycle of length 21.

A juxtaposed pair (bc, cd, ...) denotes a quantity attached to the edge joining two consecutive letters. Each letter X carries two coefficients X' and X''.

(B) The blocks. Each block is multiplied by a linear factor (x-n). For a vertex X with neighbours W, Y the block is X'(±(X-WX)) + X''(±(X-XY)). The orientation alternates:
- c, e, i, l, p, s, u (numbers 3,5,9,11,15,18,20) have the form X'(X-WX) + X''(X-XY);
- all other letters have the form X'(WX-X) + X''(XY-X).
Runs of consecutive letters of the second type share a single factor: (x-6) for f,g,h; (x-12) for m,n,o; (x-16) for q,r; (x-21) for v,a,b.
Each block also carries an extra term (last edge − first edge)·i.

The edge differences telescope around the cycle:
(cd-bc)+(de-cd)+(ef-de)+(hi-ef)+(ik-hi)+(kl-ik)+(lm-kl)+(op-lm)+(pq-op)+(rs-pq)+(st-rs)+(tu-st)+(uv-tu)+(bc-uv) = 0.
So in Σ(x-n_j)·(i-part) the coefficient of x vanishes identically (my observation).

(C) Section 'l'. Gauss writes (x-10)(l''+i) + (x-12)(l'-i) over (x-11)(l'+l''), and the condition 10(l''+i) + 12(l'-i) = 11(l'+l'').
- In general (x-a)A + (x-c)B ≡ (x-b)(A+B) as polynomials in x if and only if aA + cB = b(A+B), i.e. A(a-b) = B(b-c).
- The x-coefficients agree automatically: (l''+i) + (l'-i) = l'+l''.
- The constant terms give Gauss's condition, which simplifies (my step) to l'-l'' = 2i, i.e. l''+i = l'-i.

(D) Marginal α, β, γ computation. Gauss states that α(1-Bi) - β(1+Ai) + γ(A+B)i = 0 is equivalent to γ(A+B) = α(B+i) + β(A-i). This holds exactly when i²=-1: divide by i, using 1/i = -i. The trailing 'i' is therefore the imaginary unit, not the letter i.

(E) Section 'lm' (a 'forma 2' variant with auxiliary node quantities l^0, m^0). Three candidate pairings of the coefficient of the edge lm are listed:
- -(x-10)(l^0+l'') + (x-12)(l^0+m');
- +(x-11)(l''+i) + (x-12)(m'-i);
- -(x-11)(l''+m^0) + (x-13)(m^0+m').

The two identities written out are:
- (x-10)(l^0+l'') = (x-11)(l''+i) + (x-12)(l^0 ∓ i);
- (x-13)(m^0+m') = (x-11)(m^0+i) + (x-12)(m'-i).

For the second, the x-coefficients match identically. The constants give 13(m^0+m') = 11(m^0+i) + 12(m'-i), i.e. 2m^0 + m' = -i (my simplification).
For the first, the x-coefficients match only if the last factor is (l^0 - i). The constants then give l'' + 2l^0 = i (my simplification).

The jottings '10 11 12 / 12 10 11' record the permutation of the three factors used in the rearrangement. The final lines restate -(x-10)(l^0+l'') + (x-12)(l^0+m') and begin rewriting it in terms of (x-11) and (x-13), i.e. eliminating the factors 10 and 12 in favour of 11 and 13.
errors: In the identity (x-10)(l^0+l'') = (x-11)(l''+i) + (x-12)(l^0+i), the x-coefficients do not match as transcribed (2i surplus). It is correct only if the last factor is (l^0 - i); the manuscript sign is ambiguous/blotted.

Sign of the second 'lm' line: direct extraction of the coefficient of the edge lm from blocks (x-11) and (x-12) gives (x-11)(i - l'') + (x-12)(m' - i), not (x-11)(l''+i). The manuscript shows a blot at that sign, so this may be a slip or a different convention.
